subject: Intrinsic functions
notes: PARTIAL -> CONFORMS 2026-09-05 (kb/Work PB252). THE RECORD LISTED FOUR RESIDUES AND ALL FOUR ARE NOW CLOSED, each re-measured at HEAD rather than taken from a note. (1) STANDARD-DEVIATION / SQRT's 34-digit root: closed by PB116. MEASURED under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL on the current exe -- FUNCTION STANDARD-DEVIATION(1 2 3) = 0.816496580927726032732428024901 and FUNCTION SQRT(2) = 1.414213562373095048801688724209, i.e. the Sec.15.84.4 r2 root at 34 digits truncated by the scale-30 receiver, where the refuted path yielded the binary64 0.816496580927726 with zeros beyond. (2) FACTORIAL(34) returning the Sec.15.3 default 0: closed by PB125 -- RenderDec carries `"Factorial" when num.StandardDecimal => FactorialDec`. (3) ADDITION 2, THE MOD/REM ARMS -- THIS LANDING. PB62 moved the SUMMING family to the always-SDIDI set for exactly one reason ('the native arms first ALIGN every argument to the list's maximum scale on the Int128 carrier, so a 31-digit integer beside a scale-18 item needed 49 digits and RescaleEscape raised a size error where the SDIDI holds the answer exactly') and MOD/REM were not moved. MEASURED before the fix: `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION REM(A B)` with `A PIC 9(31)` and `B PIC 9V9(18)` terminated the run unit with EC-SIZE-OVERFLOW under STANDARD-DECIMAL, where rule 1 fixes the value at 0.5 exactly; it now returns 0.5. NOTE ON THE RECORD'S OWN WITNESS: it named MOD, and MOD CANNOT reach that state from conforming source -- Sec.15.64.3 r1 makes both arguments integers (--check OK), so MOD's common scale is always 0 and no alignment occurs; the compiler already rejects the record's own repro with COBOL1627. REM is the live half (Sec.15.77.3 r1 is 'shall be of class numeric', --check OK). MOD is routed with it because the property that decides the routing is STRUCTURAL -- the arm cross-aligns -- not because MOD had a witness. (4) THE 'SMALLER RESIDUE' ('FACTORIAL and the other non-dividing EAEs stay on the exact Int128 carrier under a standard mode, which keeps MORE than the SDIDI's 34 significant digits'): OBSOLETE AT HEAD, and re-derived rather than assumed. FACTORIAL routes to FactorialDec (PB125) and SUM to SumDec (PB62), so the EAE-bearing functions still reaching the Int128 lane under a standard mode with an all-fixed-point list are exactly ABS (Sec.15.7.4 r1), INTEGER-PART (Sec.15.49.4 r1), FRACTION-PART (Sec.15.42.4 r1) and SIGN (Sec.15.81.4 r1) -- each a single unary operation whose result is bounded by its one operand, hence at most the 31 digits the compiler's own capacity cap allows, hence exact in a 34-digit SDIDI too (Sec.8.8.1.5.2 NOTE 2). MAX/MIN/ORD-MAX/ORD-MIN carry no EAE at all (Sec.15.59.4 / Sec.15.63.4 return the CONTENT of an argument, --check OK) so rule 1 does not reach them, and INTEGER (Sec.15.44.4) has no EAE either. THE STANDARD-BINARY half of the precondition stays unreachable by design (COBOL0806) and is legitimate under Annex A.3 item 2 + Annex F.2, recorded in CONFORMANCE.md Sec.2 row 2 -- unchanged, and it was never part of the reason for the PARTIAL. STRUCTURAL GUARD: the always-SDIDI set is no longer a hand-maintained `is ... or ...` chain. Its first half is now DERIVED from the property that decides it -- IntrinsicRenderer.CrossAlignedNativeArms -- and unit:ExactCarrierBoundaryDriftTests.EveryCrossAligningNativeArm_IsRoutedToTheSdidiUnderAStandardMode reads the native switch, collects the case labels of every arm that calls AlignedArgs/AlignedArgsEx or NumericRenderer.Align against a common scale, and fails if one is missing; the failure branch was proven reachable by unrouting MOD. That is what stops this row acquiring a fifth residue the way it acquired the first four. EDITIONS carried forward as adjudicated.
